GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.2.4 p.12: supply and use are rescaled in opposite senses in an I-O quantity model, together with the export-import rescaling. S11 has no consumption volumes (agent_use_volumes), so an imbalance is measured only where exports exceed production plus imports (29 region-commodity cells on the first run, most from BACI-implied or UNSD trade volumes): P and M x g, X / g, g = sqrt(X / (P + M)). Exports with no production and no imports are set to zero. The world balance is solved with the bound domestic exports <= production, rescaling P and X in opposite senses where the world factor would lift X above P. Every moved cell is in supply_use_s11.csv and flags.csv (SUPPLY-USE-RESCALE). Since fix round w16 this one-sided rule applies only where domestic use is not measured; measured regions are balanced two-sided (energy_supply_use_balance).

GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.2.4 p.12: 'in an I-O quantity model, we rescale use and supply in opposite senses to remove supply-use imbalances, and simultaneously rescale exports and imports in opposite senses to remove export-import imbalances'; §12.2.2 discards statistical differences, so measured supply and use must meet. Measured domestic use D: crude, the refinery intake of refinery_crude_intake_cap (JODI REFINOBS, PREP crude use, UNSD 4100/086) plus the UNSD direct users of crude_direct_users.csv, where the intake is measured; coal and gas, the EIA total consumption. Regional step: supply (P, M) x a, use (D, X) / a, a = sqrt((D + X) / (P + M)). Re-exports are then removed (§12.2.5, both sides fall alike). Joint step: one world factor f per good (exports x f, imports / f, the geometric split of volume_balance) and one factor per measured region, solved together to a fixed point with the bound domestic exports <= production, so world X = world M, P + M = D + X in every measured region (S11-Hsupuse) and X <= P (S11-Hdx). Refinery intake and direct use carry the region's factor, so they add up to the crude absorption. Regions with no measured use, or whose measured use and exports are both zero, keep the one-sided rule of supply_use_balance. pet and ely are not balanced: JODI product demand includes NGL and biofuels outside PREP refinery output, and EIA electricity net consumption leaves out losses and own use, so neither is a total use (S11-Rsupuseexcl). Before/after volumes and values at S11 prices: supply_use_balance_s11.csv, S11-Rsupuse, flags SUPPLY-USE-TWO-SIDED. S11: where the domestic price rule is the IEA price gap, the domestic basic price is the reference (trade-parity) price of iea_gap_reference and fuel_subsidies_s11.csv gives the subsidy = (reference - end-user price) x domestic use (the consumption volume the gap is measured on), i.e. the region's IEA 2022 subsidy at 2022 prices (S11-Hsubsidy); S13 books it. Replaces the 2026-10-20 zero-and-flag rule (DECISION_PACK decision 5, PLAN_ERRATA E8). There the S11 price stays the consumer price, the rate is the IEA 2022 value per unit of the PREP consumption volume (the S11 absorption where PREP has none) on domestic use = the smaller of the two (step 1), rescaled to the reference price where the rate exceeds it and imports exceed half of domestic use (step 2, Table 2 rows 10-11), and the market price is consumer price + rate (PM1 = PM0 + VS/ED); the price-gap value (reference - consumer price) x use is reported beside the booked IEA value (S11-Rsubsidyext). Fix round wA (independent QA HIGH-1, 2026-10-24; David's rule "stick to GTAP"): Chepeliev et al. add the subsidy to an OBSERVED, subsidised initial price (PM1 = PM0 + VS/ED; §2.1: only subsidies that lower the consumer price below the reference). Where the S11 price is not observed (the §12.3.6 class-average fill, the import basic price) it is an unsubsidised price, and adding the IEA rate on top of it counted the subsidy twice (51 rows with the market price above the reference, about 779 bn; RUS ely 207.5 USD/MWh against a reference of 64.3). Now: an observed price (rule source_data, incl. the A9 regulated prices) stays the consumer price and the market price is that price + the rate, the rate at most the observed gap reference - price (no row where the observed price is at or above the reference); an unobserved price is replaced by the reference as the market price and the consumer price is reference - rate (fuel_subsidy_unobserved_price); the rate is at most the reference on every row (fuel_subsidy_rate_cap); S11-Hsubref (hard) checks market price <= reference, rate <= reference and consumer price >= 0 on every booked row. Fix round wA2: electricity is booked against the IEA-implied reference instead (iea_reference_ely), and a capped traded-fuel row keeps a 1 percent consumer price (fuel_subsidy_rate_cap). The w10 rule (the S11 price + the rate on every row) is the alternative every_iea_subsidy_row_gap_rows_at_reference_others_at_consumer_price_plus_harmonised_iea_rate_s13_negative_purchase_tax. basis: Fix round wA, part of fuel_subsidies. Chepeliev, McDougall and van der Mensbrugghe (2018) §3.2 step 3 add the subsidy rate to the initial market price of the GTAP data, which is an observed (I-O, subsidised) price, and §2.1 defines the subsidy as the gap between the consumer price and the reference price (international price, or supply cost where not traded). A row whose S11 price is not observed in the region (rule simple_average: the GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.6 class average of observed unsubsidised prices; rule import_basic_price: §12.3.5 CIF x (1 + duty), the trade-parity price of a net importer) has no subsidised initial price, so the subsidy is the gap below the reference: market (domestic basic) price = reference (trade_parity_reference, the same reference as iea_gap_reference and the IEA-gap rows), consumer price = reference - rate. This is the IEA price-gap rule of iea_price_gap applied with the harmonised IEA rate. Rule-1 (source_data) prices are the observed ones; IEA-gap rows are unchanged.

decided_by: Claude (fix round wA; wA2 consumer floor)
basis: Fix round wA, part of fuel_subsidies. Chepeliev et al. (2018) §3.2 step 2 (Table 2 rows 10-11) rescale an IMF rate above the GTAP FOB price to that price ("treating the GTAP-based import price as a supply cost") where imports exceed half of consumption. Here (traded fuels: coal, gas, petroleum; electricity has no cap since wA2, see iea_reference_ely) the rate is at most the reference on every row, and at most 99 percent of it where the price is not observed, so the consumer price is at least 1 percent of the reference (fix round wA2, coordinator 2026-10-24: no booked consumer price is 0; S11-Hsubcons, hard) (the import-share condition is dropped): with the market price at the reference a larger rate would give a negative consumer price, which §2.1 excludes; the independent QA (HIGH-1) found 21 rows with the IEA rate above the reference (340 bn, mostly electricity). On an observed price the rate is in addition at most reference - observed price, so the market price is never above the reference (§2.1: a consumption price higher than the reference is not a subsidy); an observed price at or above the reference books nothing (S11-Rsubsidyunbooked). The cap applied to every row and the observed-gap cap are not in the GTAP text; the rescaling to the reference is.

Fix round wA2 (replaces the wA floor of 81.1 USD/MWh, which was our number and left 15 electricity rows with a consumer price of 0). Electricity has no trade parity: Chepeliev et al. (2018) §2.1 take the supply cost as the reference of a good that is not traded, such as electricity, and GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.5-12.3.6 form no import or export parity price for it. The IEA values are kept (RUS electricity 2022 is about 90 bn real-2024 in the IEA file), so the reference is the one IEA implies: consumer price + IEA rate per unit (the paper's PM1 = PM0 + VS/ED), with no cap at our trade-parity price (reported beside it as trade_parity_price), for every electricity row with an IEA subsidy, including those the IEA gap priced before (rule 2 is not used for electricity). The consumer price is the observed S11 price (source data), else the sourced 2022 end-user tariff of config/s11/electricity_tariffs_2022.csv (BloombergNEF Climatescope average electricity price 2022 for most emerging markets; EVN, TNB, Pakistan Power Division and Taipower averages; source, URL and access date per row), else the simple average of the sourced tariffs of the region's World Bank income group (FY2023), never 0. S11-Rtariff lists the rows. The tariffs are end-user prices with taxes not separated (the electricity margin rate is 0 in Table 12.8); the income-group fill is our choice. Detail of David's IEA price-gap row (2026-10-23 19:12 UTC+7). The IEA price-gap method sets subsidy = (reference price - end-user price) x consumption, with the reference an international (trade-parity) price: export parity for exporters, import parity for importers. S11 uses its own trade prices as the reference: the region's export price where it exports more than it imports, its import basic price where it is a net importer, and the simple-average export price of the commodity where it has no trade. Where the subsidy per unit is not below that reference (S11's reference differs from IEA's), the gap is not used and the region goes to the GTAP fill; listed in S11-Rgapunused and IMPROVEMENTS_LOG S11-18.

GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.7 eq.(2): PP = (1 + MR) BP + TR. Eurostat and the EIA industrial electricity price are purchasers' prices excluding taxes, so TR = 0 and BP = PP / (1 + MR), with the Table 12.8 industrial margin rates for countries other than the US and Japan (natural gas fixed at 1.3 in the text; electricity 0). The US own I-O margin rate is not available; it only matters for US electricity, where Table 12.8 is 0. Hub and mine-gate prices are basic prices (§12.3.4) and take no margin.

GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.6 p.20: missing domestic prices are filled with the simple average of the available prices within four country classes, by whether a country is a net exporter or importer of energy and whether its energy prices are above or below average; §12.3.8 then fills what is left with the simple average of available countries. S11: net energy exporter = FOB exports above CIF imports summed over coa, oil, gas, pet and ely after the RAS; price level = mean log ratio of the region's observed basic prices to the cross-region average, over the commodities it has; a region with no observed price uses its trade class only; an empty class falls back to the all-region simple average.

decided_by: David 2026-10-25 21:13 UTC+7 (approved with the logged exceptions, after S16 and Fable QA reviews)
basis: Fable QA C-02/B-03/F-10 (2026-10-25). S11 valued domestic gas of subsidising exporters with no observed price at the 2022 export-parity reference (LBY 1,237 USD per thousand m3; 11.9 bn on a GDP of 43 bn) although the IEA's own subsidy (LBY 35 per thousand m3) implies a reference near the regulated price. Rule, for gas in the class of net energy exporters with an IEA gas subsidy: (1) PM0 = the region's observed 2022 regulated price (config/s11/transcribed_prices_2022.csv); (2) else the simple average of the class's observed prices (GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.6 class fill); (3) else, where the region's IEA rate alone is at least that average (a near-free end-use price), the lowest observed price in the region's own GTAP geographic group where one exists (ARE, KWT, IRQ: Saudi Arabia's), else the class minimum (IRN, VEN: Algeria's). The class is the net energy exporters and the net gas exporters (UZB). Market price = reference = PM0 + IEA rate (Chepeliev, McDougall and van der Mensbrugghe 2018, PM1 = PM0 + VS/ED; the IEA price-gap identity), the IEA rate uncapped so the IEA money is kept; the reference is capped at the region's own 2022 trade price (export unit value, the netback; import basic price for a net importer) where that leaves a consumer price at or above the lowest observed price, the consumer price then being that price less the IEA rate; the cap moves only an unobserved PM0, an observed regulated price stays the consumer price (Fable review). Logged departure from fix round wA (an unobserved price is unsubsidised; market never above the reference): where the IEA rate is near or above the own trade price (IRN, TKM, KAZ, UZB), domestic gas is valued above the region's own export price, because the IEA reference is a hub netback above their contract export prices (for Central Asia the 2022 IEA gap rests on a European reference) (S11-Rregref lists the rows). Reviewed by the S16 checks thread and the Fable QA thread, 2026-10-25; 'off' restores the wA rule.

Exporters whose BACI gas tonnes are estimated (gas_export_price_observed.csv) and electricity (BACI HS 271600 quantities are not TWh) stay at the reference on every route. The exporter's export price in energy_values_s11 is its VFOB over its volume (the realised price); the domestic-price rules (basic_price, exporter_price_cap, fuel_subsidies) keep the §12.3 reference price as the trade-parity price, so domestic prices move only through the import basic prices.
